notes.text: Letter headed Massy le 3.11.1970 and addressed Cher Verdier, ending Bien cordialement without a visible signature. The lower-left 15 is an archive number.
notes.basis: Observed date, salutation, closing and bottom-left pencil number; no external identification.

notes.text: The writer says he has scarcely occupied himself with Math for three months and recalls the parts still needed for SGA 4. The list has cancelled IV, par.9 et suivants, then live V and VI par.5 et suivants. A second Si je me rappelle bien qualifies the claimed completion of the overtyped Roman reference, with modifications discussed before the recipient’s departure.
notes.basis: Paragraphs 1–2 and list; reports the writer’s recollections, not verified editorial history. IV/VI order remains a source-reading doubt.

notes.text: Je pense qualifies the recipient’s possession of Saint Donat’s VI B. The writer says he sends the same person’s Appendix to XVII, has apparemment read its first pages, and asks for it to be returned to him or to St Donat with annotations and comments.
notes.basis: Paragraph 2, standalone VI B and continuation; all assertions attributed to the letter.

notes.text: Tu dois avoir presents presumed possession of a XVII impression. The letter says XVIII was typed directly on paper for offset, that the typing is finished, and that Deligne is censé to correct it.
notes.basis: Paragraph 3; these are source statements and qualifications, not independently checked facts.

notes.text: The writer requests news of the recipient’s writing and reading of VI B. For raisons techniques he would like V, VI and VI with subscript B available within deux, trois mois, and asks whether the recipient intends to finish and when. The preceding cancelled name-like word is read S[t?]inger from the surviving strokes; no publisher identity is inferred.
notes.basis: Paragraph 4; source-relative time interval and cancelled ink only.
